title: My Name
source_note: NCERT structural and thematic alignment only. All teaching passages, checks, feedback, and assessment situations are original Zidd content.

levels.title: Follow the search for a name
levels.focus: track who is asked and where the search moves next
levels.teaching_goal: Read short My Name scenes in order and match each speaker with the next helper.

guided_check.teaching_block: Read the two actions in order. The first name is the asker; the second name is the helper. Do not choose someone just because that name is nearest the question.
guided_check.passage: A worried fly asks an ant for help. The ant sends him to the old tree.
guided_check.prompt: Whom does the fly ask for help?

bridge.teaching_block: Now follow a two-step chain. Ask: who answers, and where does that answer point?
bridge.passage: The tree cannot solve the puzzle. It points toward a cow resting nearby.
bridge.prompt: Where does the tree send the fly?

masterclass.teaching_block: Keep the order straight: the place that is mentioned is not always the speaker. Match the action word with its doer.
masterclass.passage: The cow suggests the grass. The fly then hurries across the path to speak to it.

independent_check.teaching_block: Work without choices. Read once for the speaker and once for the next stop.
independent_check.passage: A beetle tells Mina to check the flower bed. Mina walks there and asks a butterfly.
independent_check.prompt: Who tells Mina to check the flower bed?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same tracking skill in a lost-and-found problem. Follow the message, not the nearest object.
transfer_check.passage: Kabir asks the bus driver about his missing cap. The driver tells him to visit the school office.

levels.title: Notice what wakes a memory
levels.focus: infer which sight or action helps someone remember
levels.teaching_goal: Connect a visible clue with the memory it brings back instead of guessing from one word.

guided_check.teaching_block: A memory clue is something seen, heard, or done that brings an idea back. Link the last event to the remembered idea.
guided_check.passage: The fly watches a dry leaf spin in the breeze. Its quick movement reminds him of how he moves through the air.

bridge.teaching_block: The clue must connect to the forgotten thing. A detail that is present but unrelated is a distractor.
bridge.passage: Leela cannot recall her dance step. When the drum begins its old beat, her feet start the step on their own.
bridge.prompt: Which clue brings the dance step back?

masterclass.teaching_block: Check cause and result. The cause comes before the words remembers or recalls.
masterclass.passage: Omar sees a blue thread tied around his pencil. He suddenly recalls that it marks the pencil his aunt gave him.
masterclass.prompt: Why does Omar remember who gave him the pencil?
accepted_answers: because he sees a blue thread

independent_check.teaching_block: Explain the link in your own words. Name both the clue and the memory; do not copy the whole passage.
independent_check.passage: Tara pauses at a gate and hears a soft bell. The sound makes her remember the bell on her puppy's collar.
independent_check.prompt: How does the sound help Tara?

concept_slots.description: State what it brings to mind.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the clue-and-memory link to a school routine. Include what is noticed and what action is remembered.
transfer_check.passage: At the end of art class, Dev sees a red sticker on the cupboard. It reminds him that red means the paintbrushes must be washed.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain what Dev remembers and why.

levels.title: Work out story words
levels.focus: use nearby actions to understand remember, shade, and breeze
levels.teaching_goal: Use a nearby result or example to infer a word's meaning in an original name-search scene.

guided_check.teaching_block: Look after the bold idea for a result. If someone can say the forgotten fact again, remember means bring it back to mind.
guided_check.passage: Nilu could not recall the tune. After one hum from Grandfather, she remembered every note.

bridge.teaching_block: Use the comfort clue. Shade is the cooler place away from direct sunlight, not the whole tree.
bridge.passage: The noon sun is hot, so the calf lies in the shade under a wide roof.
bridge.prompt: What does shade mean in this sentence?
options: a place away from direct sun
accepted_answers: a place away from direct sun
a cool place out of the sun

masterclass.teaching_block: A breeze is shown by its effect. Notice what moves gently; do not confuse it with a storm.
masterclass.passage: A light breeze lifts the corner of the name card but leaves the books still.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use both sentences. The second sentence demonstrates the target word.
independent_check.passage: Pema whispers her answer. Only the child beside her can hear it.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply context clues to a new setting. Use the action around the unfamiliar word.
transfer_check.passage: The librarian beckons to Jai by moving her hand toward herself. Jai walks to the desk.

levels.title: Choose words for a polite request
levels.focus: complete requests with ask, please, give, and thank you
levels.teaching_goal: Select courteous words that fit the speaker's purpose rather than any familiar chapter word.

guided_check.teaching_block: A polite request names what is needed and uses please. The word ask fits when we seek information.
guided_check.passage: I do not know what my name means. I will ____ my grandmother.

bridge.teaching_block: Read the speaker's purpose. Use give when an object is requested, not when a question is asked.
bridge.passage: Please ____ me the blue name card.

masterclass.teaching_block: Courtesy has an order: request first, gratitude after help. Choose the word that belongs after the action is done.
masterclass.passage: Maya returns the lost badge. Arun says, '____ you.'
masterclass.prompt: What word belongs in the blank?

independent_check.teaching_block: Complete the request without a word bank. The sentence should sound respectful.
independent_check.passage: Ria wants to borrow an eraser. She begins, '____ may I use your eraser?'

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use polite request words in a new community setting. Include both the request and gratitude.
transfer_check.passage: At a clinic, Noor needs a form from the reception desk. The receptionist hands it to him.
transfer_check.prompt: Write what Noor could say before and after receiving the form.

levels.title: Build a clear search sentence
levels.focus: arrange a doer, action, and place in sensible order
levels.teaching_goal: Reorder jumbled words by finding the doer and action before adding where or why.

guided_check.teaching_block: Start with who, then place the action beside that person. Add the place last. Capital letters can also signal the start.
guided_check.passage: Jumbled words: asks / the ant / Fly / for help
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence is in the clearest order?
options: Fly asks the ant for help.
The ant Fly for help asks.
Asks for help Fly the ant.
accepted_answers: Fly asks the ant for help.
fly asks the ant for help

bridge.teaching_block: Find the action word and ask who does it. Keep a place phrase after the main action.
bridge.passage: Jumbled words: waits / under the tree / the cow
bridge.prompt: Put the words into a sentence.
options: The cow waits under the tree.
Under waits the cow the tree.
accepted_answers: The cow waits under the tree.
the cow waits under the tree

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not begin with the action unless the sentence is a command. This sentence tells what the leaf does.
masterclass.passage: Jumbled words: across the grass / rolls / a leaf
accepted_answers: A leaf rolls across the grass.
a leaf rolls across the grass

independent_check.teaching_block: Work from meaning, not from the printed order. Use every word once.
independent_check.passage: Jumbled words: her full name / writes / Saba / neatly
accepted_answers: Saba writes her full name neatly.
saba writes her full name neatly

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same ordering skill for an announcement. Put the doer before the message action.
transfer_check.passage: Jumbled words: the next stop / announces / the conductor
accepted_answers: The conductor announces the next stop.
the conductor announces the next stop

levels.title: Introduce yourself clearly
levels.focus: share a name and one identity detail in complete sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Build a brief introduction that includes a name plus one true detail, while allowing many valid answers.

guided_check.teaching_block: A complete introduction names the speaker and gives a whole idea. A lone name is not yet a full sentence.
guided_check.passage: A new learner joins the art group. She says, 'My name is Naina. I like clay work.'
guided_check.prompt: Which choice is a complete introduction?
options: My name is Naina. I like clay work.
accepted_answers: My name is Naina. I like clay work.
my name is naina i like clay work

bridge.teaching_block: Add a detail that helps others know the speaker. Check that each sentence has a person and a complete thought.
bridge.passage: Vihaan wants to tell a classmate his name and favourite game.
options: I am Vihaan. I like kho-kho.
accepted_answers: I am Vihaan. I like kho-kho.
i am vihaan i like kho kho

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass check: choose the answer that includes both required details without adding an unrelated list.
masterclass.passage: The music teacher asks Zoya for her name and the instrument she plays.
masterclass.prompt: What is the best short reply?
accepted_answers: I am Zoya and I play the tabla.
my name is Zoya and I play the tabla
I am Zoya. I play the tabla.
i am zoya i play the tabla

independent_check.teaching_block: Write your own two-part introduction. Include the child's name and one interest; wording may differ.
independent_check.passage: Aarohi is meeting her reading partner for the first time. She enjoys funny stories.
independent_check.prompt: Write a short introduction Aarohi could give.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Create an introduction for a membership card, a new context. Include identity and one useful preference.
transfer_check.passage: Imran is joining a neighbourhood library. He loves books about space.
transfer_check.prompt: What could Imran write in the 'About me' box?

concept_slots.description: Include the kind of books he likes.

items.passage: A ladybird asks a snail for directions. The snail points to the pond.
items.prompt: Who gives the directions?

items.passage: Mohan asks the coach about a lost bottle. The coach sends him to the equipment room.
items.prompt: Where is Mohan sent?

items.passage: The sparrow questions the squirrel. The squirrel suggests asking the gardener.
items.prompt: Whom should the sparrow ask next?

items.passage: Renu speaks to the shopkeeper, who tells her to check the help desk.
items.prompt: Who tells Renu about the help desk?

items.passage: A chalk mark on the wall reminds Gopal where his team must stand.
items.prompt: What brings Gopal's memory back?

items.passage: Sia smells cardamom and recalls the sweet rice her uncle makes.
items.prompt: Why does Sia think of the sweet rice?

items.passage: A tune from the ice-cream cart makes Joel remember coins in his pocket.
items.prompt: Explain the clue and the memory.

items.passage: Nandini sees a knot on her handkerchief and remembers to return a key.
items.prompt: How does the knot help Nandini?

items.passage: The puppy dozes in the shade while the sunny steps stay hot.
items.prompt: What does shade mean here?
options: a place out of direct sun
accepted_answers: a place out of direct sun
a cool place away from the sun

items.passage: A faint breeze makes only the thin curtain move.
items.prompt: Which meaning fits faint breeze?

items.passage: Neel recalls the address after looking at the envelope again.
items.prompt: What does recalls mean?

items.passage: The teacher nods, so Pia knows she may begin speaking.
items.prompt: What does nods mean in this scene?
accepted_answers: moves her head to signal yes
moves the head to show yes

items.passage: I will ____ the caretaker where the hall is.
items.prompt: Choose the word that completes the sentence.

items.passage: '____ pass me the ruler,' said Alia.
items.prompt: Which courteous word belongs at the start?

items.passage: The guard finds Raj's bag. Raj says, '____.'
items.prompt: Write the polite words Raj should use.

items.passage: Meera needs the red folder from her partner.
items.prompt: Write one polite request she could make.

items.passage: Jumbled words: the sign / reads / Parth / carefully
items.prompt: Choose the correctly ordered sentence.

items.passage: Jumbled words: near the window / sits / the rabbit
items.prompt: Which sentence is clear?
options: The rabbit sits near the window.
accepted_answers: The rabbit sits near the window.
the rabbit sits near the window

items.passage: Jumbled words: my name / I / clearly / say
items.prompt: Put all the words in order.

items.passage: Jumbled words: opens / the office / at nine
items.prompt: Make a complete sentence.

items.passage: Kuhu joins a nature club. She likes watching butterflies.
items.prompt: Which reply introduces her clearly?
options: I am Kuhu. I like watching butterflies.
accepted_answers: I am Kuhu. I like watching butterflies.
i am kuhu i like watching butterflies

items.passage: Arman meets a new football teammate. He plays as a goalkeeper.
items.prompt: Choose the useful introduction.
options: My name is Arman, and I am a goalkeeper.
accepted_answers: My name is Arman, and I am a goalkeeper.
my name is arman and i am a goalkeeper
I am Arman. I am a goalkeeper.

items.passage: Lobsang enters a craft class. He enjoys making paper birds.
items.prompt: Write a short introduction for Lobsang.

items.passage: Sonal signs up for a science fair. She enjoys building toy bridges.
items.prompt: What could Sonal write on her name card?
